examples.ko: 그 책은 두 나라 문화를 잇는 가교 역할을 해요.
examples.en: That book acts as a bridge connecting the cultures of two countries.

examples.ko: 통역사는 서로 다른 언어 사이의 가교가 돼요.
examples.en: An interpreter becomes a bridge between different languages.

examples.ko: 그는 한국과 베트남을 잇는 가교로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: He is known as a bridge linking Korea and Vietnam.

examples.ko: 우리 동아리는 학교와 지역 사회의 가교를 맡고 있어요.
examples.en: Our club serves as the link between the school and the local community.

examples.ko: 음악은 말이 달라도 마음을 이어 주는 가교예요.
examples.en: Music is a bridge that connects hearts even when languages differ.

examples.ko: 두 팀 사이의 가교에 서 있다 보니 힘들 때도 많아요.
examples.en: Standing as the link between two teams, I often have a hard time.

explain: 일상에서 물리적인 다리는 '다리'라고 하고, '가교'는 사람, 문화, 세대를 잇는 비유로 써요. '가교 역할을 하다', '가교가 되다'가 가장 흔한 짝이에요.

phrases.example: 선생님이 학교와 집 사이에 가교를 놓았어요.
phrases.en: The teacher built a bridge between school and home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 둘 사이를 이어 주는 일을 스스로 만든다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests actively creating a link between two sides.

phrases.example: 음악은 세대 간의 가교가 될 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Music can be a bridge between generations.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이가 다른 사람들을 이어 주는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for linking people of different ages.

phrases.example: 그 사람이 두 회사 사이에서 다리 역할을 했어요.
phrases.en: That person acted as a go-between for the two companies.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가교 역할'보다 쉽고 말할 때 자연스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more natural in speech than 'gagyo yeokal'.

explain_en: For a physical bridge people say '다리'; '가교' is used figuratively for linking people, cultures or generations. The most common pairings are '가교 역할을 하다' and '가교가 되다'.

t90.ax: He is known as a bridge linking Korea and Vietnam.

examples.ko: 누리꾼들이 이 영상에 댓글을 많이 달았어요.
examples.en: Netizens left lots of comments on this video.

examples.ko: 한 누리꾼이 올린 사진이 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: A photo posted by one netizen became a hot topic.
This song is popular among netizens.
Netizens were greatly surprised after seeing the news.
The netizens' reaction was incredibly fast.
Online, netizens share information with one another.

explain: '네티즌'을 우리말로 바꾼 말이에요. 뉴스 기사에서는 '누리꾼'을 많이 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '네티즌'도 자주 써요. 온라인 댓글이나 반응을 전할 때 나오는 말이에요.

phrases.en: Netizens left a lot of comments.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 외래어예요. 일상 대화에서 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The loanword with the same meaning; heard more in daily talk.

phrases.en: Netizens' reactions to the video are heated.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 온라인 반응을 전할 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in news when reporting online reactions.

phrases.example: 그 사진은 누리꾼 사이에서 화제가 됐어요.
phrases.en: That photo became a hot topic among netizens.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인터넷에서 많은 사람이 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when many people talk about something online.
phrases.en_equiv: to be a topic among netizens

explain_en: It is the native Korean replacement for 'netizen' ('네티즌'). News articles often use '누리꾼', while everyday talk also uses '네티즌'. It shows up when reporting online comments or reactions.

en: to oppose; to clash with each other

examples.ko: 두 사람은 의견이 달라서 자주 대립해요.
examples.en: The two of them often clash because their opinions differ.
The ruling and opposition parties clashed over the bill.
There was a period when I was at odds with my parents.
Let's talk first instead of clashing.
Even though they were at odds, they eventually found a solution.
The two countries have been in opposition for a long time.

explain: 대립하다는 생각이나 입장이 서로 맞서서 부딪치는 거예요. '싸우다'는 말이나 몸으로 실제로 다투는 일이고, 대립하다는 입장이 반대라는 점을 강조해요. '의견이 대립하다'처럼 쓰고, 짝말은 '협력하다'예요.

phrases.en: The two countries opposed each other for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서로'를 붙이면 양쪽이 맞서고 있다는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 서로 makes it clear that both sides are opposing each other.

phrases.en: The two opposing people finally met.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대립하는'은 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: 대립하는 modifies the noun that follows.

phrases.en: The two of us don't have opposing opinions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 입장이 같거나 부딪치지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say that two sides agree or do not clash.

explain_en: 대립하다 is to stand against each other with opposing views or positions. '싸우다' is an actual quarrel or fight, while 대립하다 stresses that the positions are opposed. It appears in '의견이 대립하다', and its counterpart is '협력하다'.

en: to be in tune with each other

examples.ko: 두 나라의 문화는 서로 상통하는 부분이 많아요.
examples.en: The cultures of the two countries have a lot in common.
We share the same hobbies, so we became close quickly.

examples.ko: 그 두 말은 뜻이 상통하니까 바꿔 써도 돼요.
examples.en: Those two words mean much the same thing, so you can swap them.

examples.ko: 동양과 서양의 철학이 상통할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: There are times when Eastern and Western philosophy overlap.

examples.ko: 마음이 상통하면 긴 말이 필요 없어요.
examples.en: When hearts are in tune, you don't need many words.
These two stories share a common theme.

explain: '서로 통하다'라고 하면 더 쉽고 자연스러워요. '상통하다'는 글이나 발표처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 많이 쓰고, 'A와 B는 상통한다'처럼 둘이 서로 닿아 있다는 느낌으로 말해요. 마음이 통할 때뿐 아니라 생각, 뜻, 원리가 비슷할 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 우리는 생각이 서로 통해서 이야기가 즐거워요.
phrases.en: Our thoughts connect, so talking is fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상통하다'의 쉬운 말로 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, more natural everyday version of '상통하다'.

phrases.en: The two stories have something in common.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 닿아 있는 부분을 말할 때 쓰는 격식 있는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to name the points where two things connect.

phrases.en: The two proverbs have a similar meaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 다른 말이나 생각의 뜻이 이어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when different words or ideas share a meaning.

explain_en: Saying '서로 통하다' is easier and more natural. '상통하다' is used more in formal speech and writing, in the pattern 'A와 B는 상통한다'. It works for minds connecting, but also for ideas, meanings and principles that overlap.

t90.ax: These two stories share a common theme.

examples.en: The school's supporters' association prepared a scholarship.
I joined the supporters' association of a local theater troupe.

examples.ko: 후원회 덕분에 행사를 무사히 열 수 있었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the supporters' association, we could hold the event safely.
A new supporters' association to help the athletes was created.
At the association meeting, members collected money.

examples.ko: 작가의 후원회는 매달 작은 음악회를 열어요.
examples.en: The writer's supporters' association holds a small concert every month.

explain: 어떤 사람이나 단체를 돈이나 물건으로 돕기 위해 모인 모임이에요. 돕는 사람은 '후원자', 돕는 일은 '후원'이라고 해요. 같은 취미를 즐기려고 모이는 '동호회'와 달리, 후원회는 누군가를 돕는 것이 목적이에요.

phrases.en: I joined my favorite singer's supporters' association.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돕는 모임의 회원이 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when becoming a member of a supporting group.

phrases.en: The neighbors set up a supporters' association for the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돕기 위해 사람들이 새 모임을 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people start a new group to help someone or something.
phrases.en_equiv: to set up a supporters' association

phrases.en: The head of the supporters' association gave a speech at the fundraising event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 후원회를 이끄는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The title for the person who leads the association.

explain_en: 후원회 is a group formed to support a person or organization with money or goods. The supporter is 후원자 and the act is 후원. Unlike a 동호회, a hobby club for people who enjoy the same activity, a 후원회 exists to help someone.

en: to be just; to be fair; to be impartial

examples.en: A referee has to be fair to all players.
The result was fair, so no one complained.
The teacher treats students fairly.
I felt the test wasn't fair.
We decided to split the cost fairly.
If the competition is fair, I'll accept the result.

explain: '공평하다'는 똑같이 나눈다는 느낌이고, 공정하다는 규칙과 기준이 올바르다는 느낌이에요. 반대말은 '불공정하다'예요. 사람, 심판, 시험, 경쟁에 자주 써요.

phrases.en: The exam must be fair to every student.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공정하다'를 뒤의 말을 꾸미는 모양으로 바꾼 것으로, 시험이나 경쟁에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifying form, often used with exams and competitions.

phrases.en: This rule isn't fair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형이고, '불공정해요'보다 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, which sounds softer than saying 불공정해요.

phrases.en: The teacher treats all students fairly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 차별 없이 대한다는 뜻으로 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing meaning to treat people without discrimination.

explain_en: '공평하다' feels like dividing things equally, while 공정하다 feels like the rules and standards are right. The opposite is '불공정하다'. It is often used for people, referees, tests, and competition.

gh: morally right, standing up for justice

p.n: '정의롭다' would sound like the referee is a moral hero, not an unbiased judge.

examples.ko: 서양 봉건주의에서는 영주와 기사의 관계가 중요했어요.
examples.en: In Western feudalism, the relationship between lords and knights was important.
As feudalism collapsed, a new society began.
We learned about feudalism in world history class.
How are feudalism and capitalism different?

examples.ko: 그 작가는 봉건주의 사회를 비판하는 글을 썼어요.
examples.en: That writer wrote pieces criticizing feudal society.

examples.ko: 봉건주의의 영향이 아직 남아 있다는 의견이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people say the influence of feudalism still remains.

explain: 자본주의, 사회주의처럼 사회 체제를 말하는 '-주의' 말이에요. 일상 대화보다는 수업이나 글에서 주로 나오고, 말로는 '봉건 사회'나 '봉건적'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: In feudal society, social status was important.
phrases.nuance_ko: '봉건주의'를 일상에서 더 쉽게 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to refer to the world of feudalism.

phrases.en: In the age of feudalism, farmers' lives were hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시대'를 붙여 역사 속 시기를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '시대' points to a historical period.

phrases.en: That writer criticized feudalism in the novel.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-주의'는 생각이나 체제이므로 '비판하다' 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: As an '-ism', it pairs well with verbs like '비판하다'.

explain_en: Like capitalism and socialism, it is an '-주의' word naming a social system. It appears mostly in lessons and writing rather than daily talk, where people may say '봉건 사회' or '봉건적' instead.

examples.ko: 학교에서 학생을 성적으로 서열화하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Schools should not rank students by their grades.

examples.ko: 사람을 직업으로 서열화하는 시선이 아직도 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The tendency to rank people by occupation still remains.

examples.ko: 대학을 순위로 서열화한 탓에 입시 경쟁이 더 심해졌어요.
examples.en: Because universities are ranked in order, entrance competition has become fiercer.

examples.ko: 아이들을 서열화해서 비교하면 자신감을 잃기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If you rank children and compare them, they easily lose confidence.

examples.ko: 동물들은 힘으로 무리 안의 순서를 서열화하기도 해요.
examples.en: Animals sometimes set a ranking within the group by strength.

examples.ko: 학원은 학생을 점수로 서열화하지 않는다고 광고해요.
examples.en: The academy advertises that it does not rank students by score.

explain: '순서를 매기다'보다 딱딱해요. 사람이나 학교를 높고 낮음으로 가르는 상황에 써서 비판하는 느낌이 자주 있어요. 보통 '~을 ~(으)로 서열화하다'의 꼴로 써요.

phrases.en: When universities are ranked in order, competition gets fiercer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-되다'는 누군가에 의해 서열이 매겨지는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: -되다 is the passive: being put into a ranking.

phrases.en: A culture that ranks people is the problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 비판할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -는 form modifies a noun, often in criticism.

phrases.en: At the company, they rank employees by age.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 활용형이라서 일상 문장에 바로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The haeyo-style form, ready to use in everyday sentences.

explain_en: It is stiffer than '순서를 매기다'. It is used when people or schools are divided into higher and lower, often with a critical tone. It usually appears in the pattern '~을 ~(으)로 서열화하다'.

examples.en: An American governor visited Korea.
The governor announced a new plan at a press conference.

examples.ko: 그 도시는 주지사의 결정을 따를 거예요.
examples.en: That city will follow the governor's decision.
There is a student who sent a letter to the governor.

examples.ko: 새 주지사를 뽑는 선거가 다음 달에 있어요.
examples.en: The election to choose a new governor is next month.
The governor and the mayor attended the event together.

explain: '주지사'는 미국처럼 '주'가 있는 나라에서 그 주를 이끄는 사람이에요. 한국에는 '주'가 없어서 도를 이끄는 사람은 '도지사'라고 불러요. 외국 뉴스에서 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: There is a governor election next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주를 이끄는 사람을 뽑는 선거를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An election to choose the leader of a state.

phrases.en: The new governor started work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 바뀐 주지사를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news about a newly chosen governor.

phrases.en: The provincial governor attended the local festival.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국처럼 '도'가 있는 곳에서는 주지사 대신 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used instead of 주지사 where there are provinces, as in Korea.

explain_en: Head of a state, as in the US; foreign administrative unit. '주지사' is the head of a state in countries like the United States. Korea has no states, so the head of a province (도) is called a '도지사'. You hear '주지사' mostly in foreign news.

examples.en: A hearing was held at the National Assembly.
The nominee answered questions at the hearing.

examples.ko: 청문회 장면이 하루 종일 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: Scenes from the hearing were on the news all day.
This hearing will be broadcast live.
The witness who came to the hearing changed his story.
Citizens who watched the hearing posted their opinions.

explain: '청문회'는 공직 후보자나 사건 관련자에게 질문하는 공식 자리로, 뉴스에서 자주 들어요. '인사 청문회'가 대표적이에요. 보통 '청문회가 열리다', '청문회를 하다'로 써요.

phrases.example: 새 장관 후보자의 인사 청문회가 내일이에요.
phrases.en: The confirmation hearing for the new minister nominee is tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공직 후보자를 검증하는 자리를 말하는 대표적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard expression for a hearing that vets a nominee for public office.

phrases.en: The witness appeared at the hearing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불려 가서 직접 참석한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means attending in person after being summoned.

phrases.example: 국회가 이 문제로 청문회를 열기로 했어요.
phrases.en: The National Assembly decided to hold a hearing on this issue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이 청문회를 주최할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an institution organizes a hearing.

explain_en: A '청문회' is a formal session where officials ask questions of a candidate for a public post or people tied to an incident. You hear it in the news, most often as '인사 청문회'. It goes with '열리다' and '하다'.

t90.ax: This hearing will be broadcast live.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 취미가 공통돼서 금방 친해졌어요.
examples.en: The two quickly became close because they share hobbies.
These stories don't share a theme.
The two stories share a theme.

examples.ko: 두 사람 사이에 공통된 점이 하나도 없어요.
examples.en: The two have nothing in common.

examples.ko: 이 두 나라는 문화가 공통되는 부분이 많아요.
examples.en: These two countries have many parts of their culture in common.
To become friends, you need a shared topic.

explain: '비슷하다'는 모양이나 성질이 닮았다는 뜻이고, '공통되다'는 둘 이상이 함께 가진 점이 있다는 뜻이에요. '공통되는', '공통된'처럼 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태가 가장 많아요. '공통점', '공통으로'도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: We have a hobby in common.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태로, 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a noun, and the most common one.

phrases.example: 두 사람의 공통점은 음악을 좋아하는 거예요.
phrases.en: What the two have in common is that they like music.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 가진 점을 명사로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun for the point that two or more things share.

phrases.example: 이 문제는 모든 학생에게 공통으로 나와요.
phrases.en: This question appears for all students alike.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모두에게 똑같이 해당될 때 부사처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like an adverb when something applies equally to everyone.

explain_en: '비슷하다' means looking or being alike, while '공통되다' means two or more things share something. It appears most often in the noun-modifying forms '공통되는' and '공통된'. '공통점' and '공통으로' are also common.

t90.ax: The two stories share a theme.

examples.ko: 두 분수의 공통분모를 먼저 찾아야 해요.
examples.en: You have to find the common denominator of the two fractions first.

examples.ko: 우리 세 사람의 공통분모는 영화를 좋아한다는 거예요.
examples.en: The thing the three of us have in common is that we like movies.
These songs share a common thread of sadness.

examples.ko: 공통분모가 없으면 대화가 오래 이어지기 어려워요.
examples.en: Without common ground, it's hard to keep a conversation going.
I looked into what successful people have in common.

examples.ko: 분모가 다른 분수는 공통분모로 바꿔서 더해요.
examples.en: Fractions with different denominators are converted to a common denominator before adding.

explain: 수학에서는 분수 계산에 쓰고, 일상에서는 사람이나 사물이 함께 가진 점을 비유로 말할 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '공통점'이 훨씬 자주 쓰이고, 공통분모는 여러 대상을 하나로 묶는 핵심이라는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: Let's look for common ground among our different opinions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 다른 것들 사이에서 함께 가진 점을 찾는다는 비유로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used figuratively for finding what different things share.

phrases.en: The two people have nothing in common.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공통분모가 있다/없다'로 사람이나 대상이 이어지는 점이 있는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '공통분모가 있다/없다' tells whether people or things share a connecting point.

phrases.en: The two countries have a lot in common.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻으로 일상에서 훨씬 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A much more common everyday word with a similar meaning.

explain_en: Math term, figuratively the shared ground among a group. In math it is used for fractions, and in daily life it is a metaphor for what people or things share. '공통점' is much more common for the same idea, while '공통분모' feels like the key thing that ties several things together.

examples.en: Find the intersection of the two sets.
The intersection of A and B is empty.
Our tastes have almost no overlap.
The part where the two circles overlap is the intersection.
In math class we learned about intersections and unions.
I drew a picture of how big the intersection is.

explain: 반대말은 '합집합'이에요. 수학 밖에서는 취향이나 고객처럼 두 집단이 겹치는 부분을 비유로 말할 때도 '교집합이 많다/없다'라고 써요.

phrases.en: The two of us have a lot of overlap in hobbies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수학 밖에서는 겹치는 부분이 많다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Outside math, used figuratively for a lot of overlap.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a lot of overlap

phrases.example: 두 모임은 사람들이 겹치지 않아서 교집합이 없어요.
phrases.en: The two groups have no overlap because their members don't coincide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 집단이 전혀 겹치지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when two groups don't overlap at all.

phrases.example: 합집합은 두 집합을 모두 합친 거예요.
phrases.en: The union is the combination of both sets.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교집합의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '교집합'.

explain_en: Math term for items shared by two sets (교집합) Its opposite is '합집합' (union). Outside of math, people also use it figuratively for the overlap between two groups, such as tastes or customers, as in '교집합이 많다/없다'.

t90.ax: Our tastes have almost no overlap.

en: to end up as; to result in; to boil down to

examples.ko: 모든 논의는 결국 돈 문제로 귀결돼요.
examples.en: Every discussion ends up boiling down to money.
The debate ended up at the same conclusion.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 결국 교육의 질로 귀결되는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems this issue comes down to the quality of education.
I think all worries come down to health.
The negotiation ended without reaching an agreement.
I didn't know the story would end up like this.

explain: '~로 귀결되다'의 꼴로 쓰고, 이야기나 과정이 마지막에 하나의 결론으로 모인다는 뜻이에요. 토론이나 글에서 자주 나오고, 말할 때는 '결국 ~로 끝나다'라고 해도 돼요.

phrases.en: A small misunderstanding led to a big fight.
phrases.nuance_ko: '귀결되다'는 마지막에 하나로 모인다는 뜻이고, '이어지다'는 어떤 일이 다음 결과로 연결된다는 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '귀결되다' means everything ends up at one conclusion; '이어지다' is the everyday word for one thing leading to another.

phrases.en: The meeting ended up in a fight.
phrases.nuance_ko: '귀결되다'보다 말하기 편한 표현이라 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual way to say 'end up as', common in conversation.

phrases.en: This argument boils down to money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 이야기를 하나의 핵심으로 정리할 때 말로 쉽게 쓰는 꼴이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple spoken pattern for summing up many points into one key point.

explain_en: It is used as '~로 귀결되다', meaning a discussion or process finally converges on one conclusion. It is common in debates and writing, and in speech you can say '결국 ~로 끝나다' instead.

examples.ko: 형의 조용한 성격과 동생의 활발한 성격이 대조돼요.
examples.en: The older brother's quiet nature contrasts with the younger's lively one.

examples.ko: 검은 옷이 흰 벽과 대조되어 눈에 띄었어요.
examples.en: The black clothes stood out against the white wall.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 날씨가 크게 대조된다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the weather of the two countries contrasts greatly.
The mood was quiet, in contrast to the flashy stage.
Contrasting with the first part, the story got more fun.

examples.ko: 색이 서로 대조될수록 글씨가 잘 보여요.
examples.en: The more the colors contrast, the easier the text is to read.

explain: 'A와 B가 대조되다'처럼 두 가지가 나란히 있을 때 차이가 뚜렷하게 보인다는 말이에요. 조사는 '-와/과'를 써요. 사람이 비교하는 것은 '대조하다', 저절로 차이가 드러나는 것은 '대조되다'로 구별해요.

phrases.en: The two people have contrasting personalities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 많이 다른 두 가지를 설명할 때 '대조되는'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds '대조되는' to describe two things that differ greatly.

phrases.en: The colors of the two paintings contrast with each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지가 나란히 있어서 차이가 잘 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when two things side by side show a clear difference.

phrases.en: The scenery of summer and winter contrasts sharply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차이가 아주 분명하게 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the difference is very clear.

explain_en: Passive: things stand in clear contrast, differences stand out. Used as 'A와 B가 대조되다': when two things sit side by side, the difference between them stands out. The particle is -와/과. A person comparing is 대조하다; differences showing up by themselves is 대조되다.
